Title: [Popup] Copy/Paste Button
Content: List of Contents Copy/Paste Button Input Interval/Number/Position to Copy/Paste Button Duplicate Button to Symmetric Pattern Objective Copy and paste multiple buttons with keeping the interval space evenly or to Symmetric Patterns. Location Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Operation Copy/Paste Button Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Right click on an existing button, then select Copy (Ctrl+C). Right click the same button again, then select Paste (Ctrl+V). Click on a desired place to locate the copy of the button. Input Interval/Number/Position to Copy/Paste Button Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Right click on an existing button, then select Copy (Ctrl+C). Right click the same button again, then select Paste (Ctrl+V). Right click on a desired place to locate the copy of the button. The Paste window appears. Input desired value for Interval, Number of Buttons, and Position. Interval Sets the distance between buttons. Number of Buttons/Buttonholes Sets the number of buttons to copy/paste. Position Sets the position of the center of the copied button/buttonhole from the left/right/top/bottom of the pattern outline (ver2.5.0). Click OK. The buttons are now being created and applied accordingly. Duplicate Button to Symmetric Pattern Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Select a button to duplicate. The selected button is now being highlighted in yellow color. Right click on the selected button. Pop-up menu appears. Select Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern from the menu. The selected button is now being duplicated at the same level.

Title: [Property] Topstitch Corner Type
Content: List of Contents Curved Corner Right Angled Corner Objective Set Topstitch corner type to extend the stitch more smoothly at corners. Note: If stitch type is Overlock, set the corner type to Curved for smoother extension. Location Topstitch Property Editor Curved/Right Angled On / Off Operation Curved Corner Select a Topstitch with Edit Topstitch tool in the 2D window for changing its properties. Topstitch properties appear on the Property Editor. Follow the indicated guideline below: Topstitch Property Editor Curved On The selected Topstitch is now being curved and smoothly extended. Right Angled Corner Select a Topstitch with Edit Topstitch tool in the 2D window for changing its properties. Topstitch properties appear on the Property Editor. Follow the indicated guideline below: Topstitch Property Editor Right Angled On The selected topstitch is now being a right angle.

Title: Adjust Trim Weight
Content: Adjust Trim Weight - Apply weight to an OBJ trim to simulate 3D garment drape influenced by the trim. - Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern/ Edit Pattern - 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern/ Edit Pattern - Select the OBJ loaded as a trim. - Its properties appear in the Property Editor. - Simulate after entering the desired value to the Weight option. - The trim weight is applied to the Simulation.

Title: Edit Block Folders in the Modular Configurator Window
Content: Objective Edit Block folders at your convenience to organize Blocks in the folders. Location Vertical Menu Tab on the Left Modular Configurator (Select) Block Folder Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Vertical Menu Tab on the Left Modular Configurator (Select) Block Folder All Blocks in the selected Block folder appears in the Modular Configurator. Select the Edit button. Show icons appear on every Garment thumbnails. Select a Modular Structure file that you want to organize first. All Blocks compatible with the selected Module Structure are now being displayed. Click on the Display icon to either display or hide the Garments or Blocks Hidden Garments or Blocks appear in lighter shade and the displayed Garments or Blocks appear in brighter shade. Click on the Save button to save in the configuration file in the same folder as the Block. When editing is done, select the Exit button. The Blocks appear in the Modular Configurator accordingly. Note: It is able to tie the Modular configuration files as a group by adding a group in the Editor Mode when needing a category that is above all the Modular configuration files. Unlikely to the Blocks, one Modular configuration file can only be included in one group.

Title: V-Ray Render Image/Video Properties
Content: List of Contents Image/Video Properties Image/Video Image Size Color Correction Background Save Open/Save Image/Video Properties Image/Video Properties - Select the Image/Video Properties tool from the Render toolbar and navigate to the Property Editor. Image/Video - Select the medium for the final Render product among Image, Turntable Images, and Turntable Video. Image - Extract rendered 3D Garment as an image. View Point Current View - Render the 3D Garment as it is shown in the 3D window. Custom View - Render the 3D Garment with a Custom View. Render All Colorways All Colorways from the Colorway Mode are rendered(ver4.1.0). Turntable Images - Extract rendered 3D Garment as multiple images, showing it in 360. Image Count - Decide the number of images to be rendered. - Higher the Image Count is, from more viewpoints the 3D Garment is rendered. Direction Counterclockwise - The 3D Garment is rendered counterclockwise. Clockwise - The 3D Garment is rendered clockwise. Render All Colorways All Colorways from the Colorway Mode are rendered(ver4.1.0). Turntable Video - Extract rendered 3D Garment as a video rotating in 360 Video Frame Count - Decide the number of images to be rendered and stitched as a video. - Higher the Video Frame Count, more smoothly the video rotates. Duration - Decide the total duration of the video. - Expand the child menu to find Video Frame Duration, which decides the duration per frame. Direction Counterclockwise - The 3D Garment is rendered counterclockwise. Clockwise - The 3D Garment is rendered clockwise. Video Codec - Select the video codec used for recording. Render All Colorways All Colorways from the Colorway Mode are rendered(ver4.1.0). Image Size - Set the dimension of rendered images or videos. - Choose among provided presets or select Custom to freely configure the width and height of the images or videos as needed. Orientation Portrait - The image is laid out vertically. Landscape - The image is laid out horizontally. Width - Set images width Height - Set images height Maintain Ratio - Lock Width and Height ratio by toggling on the Maintain Ratio option. Color Correction Exposure - Set how much the image is exposed to light. - Higher the Exposure value is, brighter the image is. Contrast - Set how strong the bright and dark areas are contrasted. - Higher the Contrast value is, stronger the contrast gets. Background Color - Set the color of the background. Transparency - Set the background image as transparent. Save File Name - Decide the name of the saved images. File Path - Locate the saving path for the images. Open/Save Image/Video Properties Open - Open previously saved Image/Video Properties. Save - Save configured Image/Video Properties and apply to other files.

Title: [Property] 3D Seamline
Content: Objective Adjust Intensity and Thickness of 3D seamlines to render a realistic Garment. Location Main Menu Sewing Edit Sewing 3D/2D Toolbar Edit Sewing Operation Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Select a Sewing Line. Properties of the Sewing Line appears in the Property Editor. Adjust the settings below as needed: Option Description Normal Map (ver 5.2) Select an image to be used as the Normal Map. Intensity (%) Adjust the intensity of the Normal Map applied to the seamline. Thickness Adjust the thickness of the Normal Map applied to the seamline.

Title: Layer
Content: List of Contents Layer Set Layer Layer - Set the order of Layers to easily simulate layered 3D Garments. - Navigate to the Property Editor Simulation Properties Layer. Set Layer - Using the Transform Pattern tool, select the Pattern to be edited. - Navigate to the Property Editor Simulation Properties Layer. - Type in the value for the Layer option. Assign the greater value to the Patterns layered outwards. - When the Layer value is assigned, the selected Patterns will be highlighted in neon green. - Simulate to apply the setting. When Garments are completely simulated, reflecting the Layer setting, turn off the Simulation and reset Layer values of all Patterns to 0. - When Layer values is 0, Patterns are simulated according to the order placed in the 3D window.

Title: Custom Resolution
Content: List of Contents Custom Resolution Save/Open Custom Resolution Custom Resolution - Save and open customized resolution of the 3D Garment as needed. - Select the Custom Resolution tool from the 3D toolbar. Save/Open Custom Resolution - Select the Custom Resolution tool from the 3D toolbar. - The Custom Resolution widget will appear on the right top corner of the 3D window. Save Custom Resolution - Click on the Add icon on the right top corner of the Custom Resolution widget. - Current resolution will be saved and listed in the Custom Resolution widget. - The resolution includes Particle Distance, Addll Thickness - Collision/Rendering, Avatar Skin Offset, and Simulation Preset. Open Custom Resolution - Double click the saved custom resolution to return to its resolution setting while working on the 3D Garment. - The custom resolution will be reflected on the 3D Garment.

Title: Button/Buttonhole Pop-Up Menu
Content: List of Contents Button/Buttonhole Pop-Up Menu Button Right Click Pop-Up Menu Buttonhole Right Click Pop-Up Menus Button/Buttonhole Pop-Up Menu - Select desired options from the right-click pop-up menu to manage Buttons/Buttonholes. The options in the right-click pop-up menu are not applicable to fastened buttons and buttonholes. - Click on Select/Move Button tool from the 3D toolbar. Navigate to either the 3D or the 2D window and right click on the desired button/buttonhole to access the pop-up menu. Button Right Click Pop-Up Menu Reset 3D Position - Select Reset 3D Position to return the Buttons position prior to the Simulation. Copy/Paste Single Button - With Select/Move Button tool activated, right click on the button to access the pop-up menu. - Select Copy, right click again and then select Paste. - Click on the Pattern that the duplicated button will be pasted to. Multiple Buttons 3D window - To create and paste several buttons at once, select Copy and Paste, and then right-click on the Pattern. - When the Paste window appears, enter values in Interval and Number of Buttons/Buttonholes, and then hit OK. - The Button will be pasted based on the values entered. 2D window - To create and paste several Buttons at once or designate the specific paste location of the Button, select Copy and Paste, and then right-click on the Pattern. - When the Paste window appears, enter values in Interval and Number of Buttons/Buttonholes to designate the paste location, enter values in Position, and then hit OK. - The Button will be pasted based on the values entered. Mirror Paste Single Button -With the Select/Move Button tool activated, select multiple buttons to be mirror pasted. - Right-click to access the pop-up menu. Select Copy, right click again on the Buttons and then select Mirror Paste (Position Only). - Click on the Pattern that the duplicated Button will be mirror pasted to. Multiple Buttons 3D window - To create more Buttons while pasting, select Copy and Paste, and then right click on the Pattern. - When the Paste window appears, enter values in Interval and Number of Buttons/Buttonholes, and then hit OK. - The Buttons will be mirror pasted based on the values entered. 2D window - To create more Buttons while pasting, select Copy and Paste, and then right click on the Pattern. - When the Paste window appears, enter values in Interval and Number of Buttons/Buttonholes to designate the paste location, enter values in Position, and then hit OK. Delete - Select Delete to delete the selected button. - Or, hit the Delete key on the keyboard. Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern - Select Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern to duplicate Buttons to symmetric Patterns with linked editing. - For detailed instruction, reference the Index, Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern. Duplicate as Buttonhole to Symmetric Pattern - After selecting the Select/Move Button tool from the 3D toolbar, right click on the Button to be duplicated as a Buttonhole. Then, choose Duplicate as Buttonhole to Symmetric Pattern from the pop-up menu. - The selected Button will be duplicated to its symmetric Pattern as a Buttonhole. Convert to Buttonhole (ver.5.0.0) - Select the Select/Move Button tool and right click on the button in the 2D or 3D window. - Select Convert to Buttonhole from the right-click pop-up menu. - The selected button is converted to a buttonhole. Deactivate - Select Deactivate to Deactivate or Activate the selected Button. Freeze - Select Freeze to Freeze or Unfreeze the selected Button. Set Number of Sewing Layers. - Change the number of layers Buttons are sewn through. - For detailed instruction, reference the Index, Set Number of Sewing Layers. Flip - Select Flip to reverse the side of the fabric that the Button is sewn to. Buttonhole Right Click Pop-Up Menus Copy/Paste Single Button -With the Select/Move Button tool activated, right click on the Buttonhole to access the pop-up menu. - Select Copy, right click again and then select Paste. - Click on the Pattern that the duplicated Buttonhole will be pasted to. Multiple Buttons 3D window - To create and paste several Buttonholes at once, select Copy and Paste, and then right-click on the Pattern. - When the Paste window appears, enter values in Interval and Number of Buttons/Buttonholes, and then hit OK. - The Buttonhole will be pasted based on the values entered. 2D window -To create and paste several Buttonholes at once or designate the specific paste location of the Buttonhole, select Copy and Paste, and then right-click on the Pattern. - When the Paste window appears, enter values in Interval and Number of Buttons/Buttonholes to designate the paste location, enter values in Position, and then hit OK. - The Buttonhole will be pasted based on the values entered. Mirror Paste Single Button -With the Select/Move Butto tool activated, select multiple Buttonholes to be mirror pasted. - Right-click to access the pop-up menu. Select Copy, right click again on the Buttonholes and then select Mirror Paste (Position Only). - Click on the Pattern that the duplicated Buttonhole will be pasted to. Multiple Buttons 3D window - To create more Buttons while pasting, select Copy and Paste, and then right-click on the Pattern. - When the Paste window appears, enter values in Interval and Number of Buttons/Buttonholes, and then hit OK. - The Buttonholes will be mirror pasted based on the values entered. 2D window - To create more Buttonholes while pasting or designating the specific paste location of Buttonholes, select Copy and Paste, and then right-click on the Pattern. - When the Paste window appears, enter values in Interval and Number of Buttons/Buttonholes to designate the paste location, enter values in Position, and then hit OK. - The Buttonholes will be mirror pasted based on the values entered. Delete - Select Delete to delete the selected Buttonhole. - Or, hit the Delete key on the keyboard. Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern - Select Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern to duplicate Buttonholes to symmetric Patterns with linked editing. - For detailed instruction, reference the Index, Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern. Duplicate as Button to Symmetric Pattern - After selecting the Select/Move Button tool from the 3D toolbar, right click on the Buttonhole to be duplicated as a Button. Then, choose Duplicate as Button to Symmetric Pattern from the pop-up menu. - The selected Buttonhole will be duplicated to its symmetric Pattern as a Button. Set Number of Sewing Layers - Change the number of layers Buttonholes are sewn through. - For detailed instruction, reference the Index, Set Number of Sewing Layers. Convert to Button (ver.5.0.0) - Select the Select/Move Button tool and right click on the buttonhole in the 2D or 3D window. - Select Convert to Button from the right-click pop-up menu. - The selected buttonhole is converted to a button.

Title: Delete Point
Content: Delete Point - Delete points from the 2D window. - Select the Edit Pattern tool from the 2D toolbar. - Navigate to the 2D window, right click on a point and select Delete Point. - The selected point will be deleted.

Title: Create Ellipse
Content: List of Contents Ellipse Create Ellipse Ellipse - Create Ellipse or circle in 2D window. - Select the Ellipse tool from the 2D toolbar. Create Ellipse Free-hand an Ellipse - Select the Ellipse tool from the 2D toolbar, and then navigate to the 2D window. - Click and drag on the 2D window as the preview of an Ellipse appears. - Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to create a Circle. - When the desired shape of an Ellipse or a Circle is achieved, release the mouse. - An Ellipse or a Circle Pattern is created based on the settings. Use Diameter &amp Radius - Select the Ellipse tool from the 2D toolbar, and then navigate to the 2D window. - Click on the 2D window. The Create Ellipse Window appears. - Enter desired values for Width, Height, Diameter, and Radius. Then, hit OK. - An Ellipse or a Circle Pattern is created based on the settings. Use Circumference - Select the Ellipse tool from the 2D toolbar, and then navigate to the 2D window. - Click on the 2D window. The Create Ellipse window appears. - Enter desired values for Circumference. - An Ellipse or Circle Pattern is created based on the settings. Create and Replicate Ellipses - Select the Ellipse tool from the 2D toolbar, and then navigate to the 2D window. - Click on the 2D window. The Create Ellipse window appears. - Interval: type in the distance between the Ellipses. - Angle: type in the angle that replicated Ellipses will be created. - Number of Shapes: type in the number of Ellipses to be replicated. - Click OK. - The Ellipses are created based on the settings above.

Title: [CLOSET] File Sharing via CLOSET
Content: Objective Upload 3D files and share them easily with others. Location Main Menu File Share Project/Garment Main Menu icon Project/Garment Operation Construct a Garment. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Share Project/Garment Main Menu icon Project/Garment You will be directed to the Upload page in CLOSET. If you are not a registered member of CLOSET, you are directed to the Sign Up page. Note: For detailed instruction on how to use CLOSET, please refer to the attached manual.

Title: Edit AI Bezier Curve
Content: List of Contents Edit Curvature Convert a Segment Point to an AI Bezier Curve Delete Handles Objective Edit AI Bezier curves with editing tools. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Curve Point or Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Curve Point or Edit Pattern Operation Edit Curvature Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Curve Point or Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Curve Point or Edit Pattern Click the point on the AI Bezier Curve to access the handle. When the handle appears, click and drag the point on the desired end of the handle to change the curvature. Note: To edit only one side's curvature, hold down the Alt key on the keyboard while click and dragging the point on the desired end of the handle. To maintain the handle's angle while changing the curvature, press down the Ctrl key on the keyboard then click and drag the curve. (ver.5.1.0) Convert a Segment Point to an AI Bezier Curve Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Curve Point or Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Curve Point or Edit Pattern To convert a Segment Point to an AI Bezier curve, hold down the Alt key on the keyboard, and then click and drag the desired Segment Point. The selected Segment Point is converted to an AI Bezier curve as the blue handle appears. Delete Handles Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Curve Point or Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Curve Point or Edit Pattern Click the Segment Point on the curve. The pair of handles appear. Right click on the point on the desired handle to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Delete Point. Or, hit the Delete key on the keyboard. The selected handle is deleted and the curve is converted to a straight line. Note: To delete the pair of handles at once, hold down the Alt key on the keyboard and select the Segment Point on the curve.

Title: Project File (ZPRJ) Open/Add/Save
Content: List of Contents Open or Add Save Objective All information, including garments, avatars, 3D environments(background, lighting, wind, camera and simulation), animatiands, and so on, can be saved and loaded as one project file(ZPRJ). Location Open/ Add Main Menu File Open/Add Project Save Main Menu Save/Save As Project / Project (with Other Files) Operation Open or Add Select the tool indicated in Location. The Open Project window appears. Navigate and select the Project file to be added and click Open. The project file is loaded immediately. If you have already imported files or are importing additional files, the Open Project window appears. Apply any detailed settings, then click on the OK button. Option Description Load Type Open a new project file or add the file additionally. Note:If you add additional files, you can set the position of the object in the X, Y, and Z axis. Object Select the items to load within the project file. Items that are not included will be disabled. Note: You can load the project file directly by dragging it from the file explorer window to the 3D window. You can add it by right-clicking on the project file in the Library window and clicking the Add to Workspace menu. Save Select the tool indicated in Location. The Save Project window appears. Set the location and name to save and click the Save button. The project file will be saved in the location. A preview image is displayed in the saved project file thumbnail. (ver 2024.0) When saving as a project &amp other files, select the files (Texture, DXF, PDF) to be saved together and click the OK button. A folder is created with the path and name you set, and each file is stored together in the folder.

Title: Avatar Right-Click Pop-Up Menu
Content: Objective Set the Avatar via the right-click pop-up menu. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move Operation Select the tool/menu indicated. Right Click on the avatar and set the options as needed. Option Descriptions Select All Faces Select all surfaces of an Avatar. Move Avatar&ampGarment Select and Move both avatar and garment. Delete Avatar Select an avatar and delete it. Move Avatar/ Move All Avatars &amp Garments Move Avatar or all Avatars and garments to the center of the 3D window or the ground. Reset Joints Reset joints of the Avatars. Change Heels Make Avatars' heels up or down. Deactivate/Activate Avatar Deactivate or activate avatars as needed. When it is deactivated, the garments do not recognize while simulation. Deactivate/ Hide (ver 7.1) Deactivate and Hide the selected part of the Avatar at the same time. Show/Hide All Avatars Show or hide individual or all avatars.

Title: Copy Buttonhole Style
Content: Objective Copy and modify a buttonhole in order to create a new buttonhole style or adjust its properties. Location Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Copy Operation Navigate to the Object Browser and select an item in the buttonhole tab. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Copy A new buttonhole item with the same properties of the selected item is now being created.

Title: Skive
Content: Objective Add skiving effect on desired parts of a Pattern or all Patterns (ver2.3.0). Location Property Editor (Internal Shapes/Pattern Only) Bond/Skive Skive Operation Select a pattern or an internal shape to express skiving with Edit Pattern or Transform Pattern tools. Its properties appear in Property Editor. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor (Internal Shapes/Pattern Only) Bond/Skive Skive The select Pattern/Internal Shape is now being displayed in a semi-transparent grey color. A scrollbar appears, displaying the physical property of the pattern from the value range of one ('1') to one hundred ('100') in Percentage (%). Move the scrollbar to adjust as desired. Activate the Simulate. The area of the internal shape is now being displayed softer as if it has been shaved down.

Title: [Property] Create 2D Button Measurement
Content: Objective View button position from the Pattern outline with 2D measurements (ver2.5.0). Location Object Browser Button Property Editor 2D Measurements To Center Operation Select a button with Select/Move Button tool in the 3D toolbar. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Button Property Editor 2D Measurements To Center Select the desired 2D measurement options of the left/right/up/down. The 2D measurement is now being displayed or hidden accordingly.

Title: [2D Tool] Check Sewing Length
Content: Objective Check significant difference in Sewing Line lengths. You can check unintended Sewing Line length difference made during the garment making process. Location Main Menu Sewing Check Sewing Length 2D Toolbar Check Sewing Length Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Check Sewing Length 2D Toolbar Check Sewing Length The Sewing Lines with length difference (default: 5mm) are bolded and highlighted in red.

Title: Open/Save Blocks
Content: List of Contents Open Save Objective Open and save Block component files (.ZBLC). Location Modular Mode Block Editor Operation Open Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode Block Editor Mouse over on a desired Modular Template. Open button appears. Click Open button to load Block files. Save Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode Block Editor Mouse over on a desired Modular Template. Save button appears. Click Save button. A pop-up window appears. Select a desired location with a desired file name and click Save button. Save Block Component window appears. Set additional settings as the following menu below if needed: Thumbnail Use Block Component Thumbnail A default thumbnail image. Create New Thumbnail Select an image for the thumbnail. The file is now being saved and appeared in the Modular Configurator.

Title: Shrink Pattern
Content: Objective Shrink or stretch 3D Garment Pattern horizontally and vertically without changing it in the 2D Pattern window. The default value is 100 percent (%) which indicates the natural state of the Garment material, in other words there is no artificial shrinkage or stretchiness. Use the function to express shrinkage after textile treatments such as garment washing, or use it temporarily to draw the inner layer against the avatar when dressing multiple layers of Garments for easier Simulation. Location Click Pattern Property Editor Simulation Properties Shrinkage Weft/Warp Operation Select a Pattern to shrink with 2D toolbar's Edit Pattern or Transform Pattern. Follow the indicated guideline below: Click Pattern Property Editor Simulation Properties Shrinkage Weft/Warp Enter desired shrink values. The Pattern in the 3D window is now being shrunk accordingly.

Title: Window Layout
Content: Use the buttons on the lower right-hand corner of the screen to switch between different layout configurations for the 3D and 2D Windows (ver2.3.0.)

Title: Delete Curve Point
Content: Objective Delete unnecessary curve points when editing Patterns. When all curve points on a segment is deleted, it turns to a straight line. Location Delete Selected Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Curve Point 2D Toolbar Edit Curve Point Delete All Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Segment) Delete All Curve Points Operation Delete Selected Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Curve Point 2D Toolbar Edit Curve Point Right click on the curve point to be deleted and select Delete on the pop-up menu. Or, select the curve point and hit Delete key on the keyboard. Note: Multiple curve points cannot be moved at once for now due to technical limitation. When you delete a segment point added on a curved line, all curved points on that specific line are deleted and so as the curvature. Delete All Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the Edit Pattern tool. Then, select a segment which all curved points should be deleted. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Segment) Delete All Curve Points All curve points on the selected segment are deleted.

Title: Unfold
Content: Objective Unfold a half pattern as a full pattern with no center line or seam. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Operation Click the tool/menu indicated. Right-click on the fiducial segment of the pattern, and click Unfold menu. The selected pattern and internal polygon are unfolded symmetrically. Or if you only want to unfold the pattern except for the internal lines or base lines, click Unfold Pattern Outline Only menu. Only the pattern unfolds, with the internal polygons and baselines located on one side. (ver 7.2) Note: You can unfold multiple patterns at once by selecting the center lines of the patterns at the same time. (ver 7.2)

Title: Roll Up Selected Area
Content: Objective Roll up selected area horizontally or vertically. Location Selected Area Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Roll Up Horizontally / Roll Up Vertically Operation Select a desired area to flip, with Select Mesh tool. Follow the indicated guideline below: Selected Area Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Roll Up Horizontally / Roll Up Vertically Activate the Simulate tool. The selected area is now being flipped over horizontally or vertically.

Title: Edit Measure (Avatar) Option
Content: List of Contents Edit (ver 7.1) Option Objective Set options for the Measure(Avatar). Location 3D Toolbar Edit Measure (Avatar) Operation Edit (ver 7.1) Select the tool/menu indicated. Click and drag the point of the tape measure to move it. The points on the tape measure are moved. Option Right-click on the Tape Measure and set the options below. Delete Measure Delete the Tape Measure Duplicate to Symmetric Position Duplicate the tape measure to the symmetrical position of the avatar. Show/ Show All Length The selected tape measure or the length of the entire tape measure is shown or hidden.

Title: Subsurface Scattering Material
Content: Objective Realistically express human skin. Subsurface Scattering Material penetrates and scatters under the objects' surface. Utilize the material to illustrate leaves, fruit, candles and more. Application results are only be viewed in the Render window. Watch Tutorial Video Location Fabric Property Editor Material Type Skin (Render Only) Operation Select the menu/tool indicated. Refer to the table below to edit the properties. Properties Description Mix Adjust the value of Subsurface Scattering (in which light is scattered by penetrating objects). If the value is 0, the material is not applied and is reflected only on the surface of the object. If the value is 1, it is applied to the maximum extent and does not reflect on the surface of the object. Mix Map (ver 7.1) Apply a Mix Map to partially apply the amount of subsurface scattering. Density Scale Adjust the size property of an object to adjust the extent to which SSS is applied. The smaller the value, the wider the SSS coverage. Note: The Density Scale is applied by multiplying/sharing of each layer radius value, so adjust only the size to which SSS is applied while maintaining the radius ratio between the three layers. Shallow / Medium / Deep Adjust the properties of the three layers of subsurface scattering to express composite materials. Color Set the color of the light to be scattered. Color Map Use a map to express the desired color in the desired area. Weight The weight of the layer sets the intensity of the color and map of the layer that is set against the other layer. If the value is 1, it has the highest weight. Radius Set the radius in which each layer scatters inside the surface of the object. Start the Render window. Subsurface Scattering Material materials are applied. Note: When two or more meshes are overlapped, SSS materials can appear abnormally. Therefore, take the overlapped meshes off each other using other 3D programs, or import the meshes separately and apply SSS materials.

Title: How to Fix the Error using Intel Graphics Card
Content: List of Contents Case 1 Case 2 (If the error is not resolved by Case 1) Objective Learn how to resolve launching error using Intel HD Graphics. Operation Since this crashing is due to a Graphic driver which is automatically updated by Microsoft Windows, please re-install the Intel graphics driver after deactivating "Windows Automatic Updates". Case 1 Please input "gpedit.msc" on Search tool and execute it. Local Group Policy Editor Computer Configuration Administrative Templates Windows Components Windows Updates activate "Do not include drivers with Windows Update" Note: The option may not appear in the Window versions below. In this case, External Graphics card should be used. (Please refer to Computer Specification) Windows 7 Home Edition / Windows 10 Home Edition Device Manager Display Adapters Intel(R) HD Graphic Uninstall the device and driver software Reboot Windows Enter Intel Support Page and download and install the program of Intel Driver &amp Support Assistant. Start scanning the driver. Download and Reinstall the driver of Intel(R) HD Graphics. Verify the "23.20.16.4901" version is installed correctly. Please reboot Windows. If the Error is not resolved with Case 1, please proceed Case 2 below. Case 2 If the Error is not resolved with Case 1, please proceed Case 2. Please enter Intel Graphics Driver for Windows* and Download &amp Install the driver. Approve overwrite to the previous version during Installation.
